Key right. POL-RD-01 establishes the deviation and licenses PARTIAL_REFUND; POL-RD-02 fixes the amount and licenses PARTIAL_REFUND; POL-RD-13 decides that the uncited accident excuse is discarded, that POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and that POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal (licenses PARTIAL_REFUND); POL-RD-09(1) applies because off-route ERP exists and must not be added on top. POL-RD-06 applies: its rule says the driver_profile is consulted whenever POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation, and 55.40 % > 50 % is material, so the check is mandatory even though it finds no pattern; POL-GEN-01 governs that read (lifetime prior_deviation_flags 7 is context only, and misreading it is the live uplift trap). Reader A's omission of POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 is the reader's error, not the key's - both clauses do apply. Both readers' extra POL-RD-08 is a harmless addition (it licenses PARTIAL_REFUND and is the burden rule POL-RD-13 refers to), but POL-RD-13 already states the consequence that decides the case, so its absence from the key is not an error. No clause in the key fails to apply.

Key right. Neither REVERSAL nor INDETERMINATE fits: the trace corroborates the filing rider (CTE then PIE, about 2.79 km beyond the dropoff and back), and the driver's excuse is discarded as uncited rather than contradicted (POL-RD-13(1) itself calls an uncited missing advisory a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction); the ruling is not ESCALATE. Between EASY and HARD the case carries several outcome-changing steps, each of which a reader can get wrong: (i) the POL-RD-10(5) vs POL-RD-13 tension over a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory (both readers recorded it as their main doubt; misread, it escalates with no money); (ii) materiality rests on the percentage limb only (7.701 km < 8.0 km) and then requires the POL-RD-06 check, where the lifetime prior_deviation_flags 7 would, if misused as the 90-day counter, produce a FULL_REFUND uplift; (iii) surge must be read from the fare breakdown (ignoring it gives 21.90); (iv) the 3.50 off-route ERP must not be added on top (19.25). Readers who solved it correctly calling it easy is an opinion, not a policy error; HARD is a correct label for a multi-clause case with an amendment-resolved conflict and several live traps.

POL-RD-05 (no amendment fields), POL-RD-11 (METERED, quoted_fare_sgd null) and POL-RD-12 (RYDE_PLUS) do not apply. (2) Same trip (POL-RD-08(a)): TRP-04015 on trip record, trace and fare; first fix 18:41:30 = started_at and lies 0 m from the pickup pin; last fix 19:16:40 = ended_at = fare charged_at and lies 0 m from the dropoff pin. (3) POL-RD-07: 212 fixes, every interval exactly 10 s, largest step 133.4 m, highest implied speed 48.0 km/h, accuracy 3.0-7.9 m - no limb (a)-(c) met; trace weight 1.0. (4) POL-RD-01: recomputed trace length 21.60082 km, written 21.601; excess 21.601 - 13.9 = 7.701 km = 55.4029 % of optimal; > 20 % (2.78 km) and > 0.8 km so ESTABLISHED; > 50 % so MATERIAL (absolute 7.701 < 8.0). Not knife-edge: even the forbidden 21.6 copy gives 7.7 km = 55.40 %. (5) POL-RD-13: the driver asserts an accident near Marine Parade (an incident, so within RD-13's 'external traffic cause'); the counterparty statement names no evidence id; EV-ADVIS-04015-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0. RD-03 is unavailable, the assertion carries no weight (POL-RD-08), RD-13(1) takes the case outside POL-RD-10(5), and RD-13(2) applies because the rider's excess stands on an unimpaired trace: the deviation stands at the measured figure and RD-02 runs on the booked optimal. Both readers raised whether the minted id in dispute.evidence_ids counts as the driver 'citing' it; RD-13(1) turns on whether the asserting party names the id, the driver's statement names none, and RD-13's notes describe exactly this pattern (an identifier minted so its absence can be cited, with an uncited driver traffic excuse) as settled by an ordinary RD-02 refund. Not a genuine second answer, so no case fix. (6) POL-RD-06 (material): deviation_flags_90d 1 (< 3), 1/412 = 0.00243 (< 0.05, completed_trips_90d >= 40): no pattern, no uplift, no referral; prior_deviation_flags 7 is lifetime and barred by RD-06 and POL-GEN-01. (7) POL-RD-02 (METERED): surge_multiplier 1.3 from EV-FARE-04015; on-route ERP 0.00 (trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd and the route_planned event); airport 0.00, waiting 0.00, promo 0.00. recomputed = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.9 + 0.28 x 22) x 1.3 + 0.80 = 20.385 x 1.3 + 0.80 = 27.3005. Both lie off the optimal route (on-route ERP 0.00), so under RD-09(1) the 3.50 is already comprehended in 15.75 and is not added. (9) POL-RD-10: no trigger. (1) deciding artifacts EV-GPS-04015, EV-TRIP-04015, EV-FARE-04015 and EV-DPROF-04015 all weight 1.0; EV-RPROF-04015 (STALE_SNAPSHOT 0.75) decides nothing because deviation_claims_60d is 0 and the excess is above 30 %; (2) ids match; (3) trace clean; (4) no timestamp disagreement; (5) not engaged per RD-13(1); (6)-(8) not engaged as above.
